question: Cyber exercises invoking the mutual defence clause under Article 42(7) TEU

As part of the ‘EU CyCLES’ exercise, Member States tested their response to attacks with significant kinetic effects and casualties under the mutual defence clause of Article 42(7) TEU. For the first time, a simulation was carried out in which the threshold of an armed attack was surpassed. 1.

In which cyber exercises, in which the Council participated or which it coordinated in working parties over the last three years, was invoking the mutual defence clause under Article 42(7) TEU simulated?
What cyber exercises is the Council planning for 2024, and which of these exercises involve invoking the mutual defence clause under Article 42(7) TEU?
In the Council’s view, what objective factors must be present for the mutual defence clause under Article 42(7) TEU to be invoked in response to a cyber attack?
answer: Over the last three years there has been only one cyber exercise organised in the Council which simulated the invoking of the mutual defence clause of Article 42(7) TEU.

This exercise (called EU CyCLES, Cyber Crisis Linking Exercise on Solidarity) was organised in 2022 under the French Presidency of the Council of the European Union, together with the European External Action Service (EEAS) and the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).

In the context of the EU Integrated Resolve 2022 Parallel and Coordinated Exercise (EUIR22 PACE), Council reactions and procedures on major aspects of response, such as the EU’s response to an invocation of the Solidary Clause (Art. 222 TFEU) and the Mutual Assistance clause (Art. 42.7 TEU), were tested.

The relevant Council Working Parties also exercised their relevant procedures in the framework of this PACE exercise. Further cyber exercises are envisaged and carried out in the Council structures in 2024.

However, the information requested by the Honourable Member on their planning or a possible inclusion of the mutual defence clause (Article 42(7) TEU) as a component of these exercises is not available at this stage. Each year, the Presidency of the Council and the EEAS organise the EU Cyber Diplomacy Toolbox (CDT) Exercise to test agreed procedures.

The purpose is to exchange situational awareness, implement measures, familiarise all relevant stakeholders with the CDT’s Implementing Guidelines and identify potential areas of improvement. The content of the next CDT is to be discussed with the Presidency of the Council.
